- theme-factory: Toolkit for styling artifacts with a theme. These artifacts can be slides, docs, reportings, HTML landing pages, etc. There are 10 pre-set themes with colors/fonts that you can apply to any artifact that has been creating, or can generate a new theme on-the-fly.

content.text:
Yes. Bug.

`<Trans id="dashboard.sidebar.header.kanban">Kanban</Trans>` exists in code, but the id is missing from `packages/i18n/locales/en/messages.po`. Lingui's babel macro strips the inline fallback text in production builds → renders raw id.

Four more `<Trans>` ids have same problem and will show raw ids too:
- `dashboard.sidebar.header.kanbanTooltip`
- `workspace.addTabMenu.chat`
- `workspace.missingWorktree.archiveWorkspace`

--- glossary ---
# Translation glossary

Input for translators, reviewers, and the translation CI prompt. Policy
(Kiet, 2026-08-27): **product vocabulary translates — except the word
"Superset" itself, which is never translated or transliterated in any
locale.** "Workspace", "agent", "pane", "task", "automation", and the rest
are rendered in each locale's natural term, not kept as English islands.

## Never translated

These are literal identifiers, not vocabulary:

- **Superset** (brand), product names of third-party agents and tools
  (Claude, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, GitHub, Linear, Slack, ...)
- CLI commands and flags (`superset ws create`, `--json`), file paths,
  environment variables, code identifiers
- Keyboard keys and chords (⌘K, Ctrl+Shift+P)
- Protocol/standard names (MCP, tRPC, SSH, PR in `git`-context UI strings is
  translated per locale convention; see per-term notes below)

## Per-term guidance

| Term | Guidance |
|---|---|
| workspace | Translate with the locale's standard software term (e.g. ja: ワークスペース, zh-CN: 工作区). Must be used consistently everywhere, including onboarding and docs. |
| agent | Translate/transliterate per locale convention for AI agents (ja: エージェント, zh-CN: 智能体 or 代理 — pick one per locale and keep it). |
| pane | The locale's standard split-view/pane term. |
| pull request / PR | Follow the locale's developer convention (ja and zh commonly keep "PR"/"プルリクエスト"). |
| terminal | The locale's standard term for a terminal emulator. |
| host / host service | Translate "host" only where it reads as a common noun; "host-service" as a component name stays English. |

Add a row whenever a translation review settles a disputed term; this file
rides along in the LLM translation prompt, so rows here are enforcement, not
documentation.

content.content:
### dashboard.automations.hostOfflineHelp
ja	ホストがSupersetリレーに接続されていません。このデバイスの場合は、設定 > リモートアクセスで「リレー経由でこのデバイスへのリモートアクセスを許可」をオンにしてから再試行してください。
zh-CN	该主机没有连接到Superset中继。如果就是此设备，请在“设置>远程访问”中打开“允许通过中继远程访问本设备”，然后重试。
fr	L'hôte n'est pas connecté au relais Superset. S'il s'agit de cet appareil, activez « Autoriser l'accès distant à cet appareil via le relais » dans Paramètres > Accès distant, puis réessayez.
ko	호스트가 Superset 릴레이에 연결되어 있지 않습니다. 이 기기라면 설정 > 원격 액세스에서 \"원격 액세스가 릴레이를 통해 이 기기에 접근하도록 허용\"을 켠 뒤 다시 시도하세요.
zh-TW	該主機沒有連線到Superset中繼。如果就是此裝置，請在「設定>遠端存取」中開啟「允許遠端存取通過中繼存取此裝置」，然後重試。
es	El host no está conectado al relay de Superset. Si es este dispositivo, activa \"Permitir que los espacios de trabajo remotos accedan a este dispositivo mediante el relay\" en Configuración > Acceso remoto y vuelve a intentarlo.
de	Der Host ist nicht mit dem Superset-Relay verbunden. Falls es dieses Gerät ist, aktiviere \"Fernzugriffn den Zugriff auf dieses Gerät über das Relay erlauben\" unter Einstellungen > Fernzugriff und versuche es erneut.
pt-BR	O host não está conectado ao relay do Superset. Se for este dispositivo, ative \"Permitir acesso remoto a este dispositivo via relay\" em Configurações > Acesso remoto e tente novamente.
it	L'host non è connesso al relay di Superset. Se è questo dispositivo, attiva \"Consenti l'accesso remoto a questo dispositivo tramite relay\" in Impostazioni > Accesso remoto, poi riprova.
ru	Хост не подключён к реле Superset. Если это текущее устройство, включите «Разрешить удалённый доступ к этому устройству через реле» в Настройки > Удалённый доступ и повторите.
tr	Host, Superset rölesine bağlı değil. Bu cihazsa Ayarlar > Uzaktan erişim bölümünde \"Uzaktan erişimnın bu cihaza röle üzerinden erişmesine izin ver\" seçeneğini açıp yeniden deneyin.
pl	Host nie jest połączony z przekaźnikiem Superset. Jeśli chodzi o to urządzenie, włącz „Zezwól na zdalny dostęp do tego urządzenia przez przekaźnik” w Ustawienia > Dostęp zdalny i spróbuj ponownie.

content.content:
name: Build Windows ARM64 (vendored fork)

# Self-repairing build of the vendored fork source at repo root.
# The build steps themselves are deterministic and live in
# .github/actions/arm64-build (thin shims over scripts/) — this file only
# orchestrates a bounded attempt/repair loop:
#
#   build-attempt-1 ──fail──> repair-1 (Opus 5) ──> build-attempt-2
#                                   ──fail──> repair-2 (Opus 5) ──> build-attempt-3
#
# Max 3 build attempts / 2 AI repairs, then verdict fails LOUD. Every repair
# is pushed to the repair branch (nightly candidate, or the dispatched branch
# for manual runs) and the next attempt builds that exact sha, so every
# deterministic gate re-runs on the repaired tree. (BUILD-REPAIR)
#
# Why the split matters: workflow YAML is frozen when a run starts and
# GITHUB_TOKEN cannot push .github/workflows changes — but .github/actions/**
# and scripts/** are ordinary repo files, checked out per attempt, so the
# repair AI can fix ~everything mid-run. Workflow-YAML fixes need the
# WORKFLOW_PUSH_TOKEN secret (fine-grained PAT, Contents+Workflows write) and
# take effect the NEXT run.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      publish:
        description: 'Publish the desktop-v<version> Release (rebuilt in place; one version, no beta)'
        type: boolean
        default: true
      repair_branch:
        description: 'Branch AI repairs are pushed to (default: the dispatched branch)'
        type: string
        default: ''
  # Reusable so nightly-merge.yml can invoke the exact same build.
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      publish:
        type: boolean
        default: false
      ref:
        description: 'Git ref to build (default: the triggering ref)'
        type: string
        default: ''
      repair_branch:
        description: 'Branch AI repairs are pushed to (nightly passes the candidate)'
        type: string
        default: ''
    outputs:
      built_sha:
        description: 'The exact commit the successful attempt built (differs from the input ref when a repair landed)'
        value: ${{ jobs.verdict.outputs.built_sha }}

permissions:
  contents: write
  actions: read # repair jobs download this run's failed-job logs

name: Build Windows ARM64 (vendored fork)

# Self-repairing build of the vendored fork source at repo root.
# The build steps themselves are deterministic and live in
# .github/actions/arm64-build (thin shims over scripts/) — this file only
# orchestrates a bounded attempt/repair loop:
#
#   build-attempt-1 ──fail──> repair-1 (Opus 5) ──> build-attempt-2
#                                   ──fail──> repair-2 (Opus 5) ──> build-attempt-3
#
# Max 3 build attempts / 2 AI repairs, then verdict fails LOUD. Every repair
# is pushed to the repair branch (nightly candidate, or the dispatched branch
# for manual runs) and the next attempt builds that exact sha, so every
# deterministic gate re-runs on the repaired tree. (BUILD-REPAIR)
#
# Why the split matters: workflow YAML is frozen when a run starts and
# GITHUB_TOKEN cannot push .github/workflows changes — but .github/actions/**
# and scripts/** are ordinary repo files, checked out per attempt, so the
# repair AI can fix ~everything mid-run. Workflow-YAML fixes need the
# WORKFLOW_PUSH_TOKEN secret (fine-grained PAT, Contents+Workflows write) and
# take effect the NEXT run.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      publish:
        description: 'Publish the desktop-v<version> Release (rebuilt in place; one version, no beta)'
        type: boolean
        default: true
      repair_branch:
        description: 'Branch AI repairs are pushed to (default: the dispatched branch)'
        type: string
        default: ''
  # Reusable so nightly-merge.yml can invoke the exact same build.
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      publish:
        type: boolean
        default: false
      ref:
        description: 'Git ref to build (default: the triggering ref)'
        type: string
        default: ''
      repair_branch:
        description: 'Branch AI repairs are pushed to (nightly passes the candidate)'
        type: string
        default: ''
    outputs:
      built_sha:
        description: 'The exact commit the successful attempt built (differs from the input ref when a repair landed)'
        value: ${{ jobs.verdict.outputs.built_sha }}

permissions:
  contents: write
  actions: read # repair jobs download this run's failed-job logs

1	<!-- ===================================================================== -->
2	<!-- FORK MAINTENANCE (khairm Windows ARM64 fork). Everything ABOVE the -->
3	<!-- divider is about maintaining this fork; everything BELOW is upstream  -->
4	<!-- superset's own developer guide, unchanged, for working on the app.    -->
5	<!-- ===================================================================== -->
6	
7	# superset-windows-arm64 — Windows ARM64 fork maintenance
8	
9	This repo is a **vendored fork** of [superset-sh/superset]: the full upstream
10	source with our Windows ARM64 + feature changes committed on top, plus CI that
11	builds a native **Windows ARM64** one-click NSIS installer. The fork is the
12	source of truth; we track upstream by **merging its deltas**, not by
13	re-applying changes. `.fork/upstream-baseline.txt` records the upstream
14	`desktop-v*` tag the baseline currently sits on.
15	
16	## Setup / architecture (high level)
17	
18	- **Build (deterministic steps, self-repairing).** `.github/workflows/build-arm64.yml`
19	  orchestrates a bounded attempt/repair loop `(BUILD-REPAIR)`: the actual build
20	  steps (install → compile → materialize the win-arm64 native closure
21	  (`scripts/materialize-native-closure.sh`: libsql/tokenizers/node-pty) →
22	  package the installer → verify packaged natives are ARM64 → publish) live in
23	  `.github/actions/arm64-build/action.yml` as thin shims over `scripts/*.sh`.
24	  A failed attempt triggers an Opus 5 (`claude-opus-5`, effort high) repair job
25	  that reads the failed log, fixes the checked-out tree, and pushes to the
26	  repair branch (nightly candidate / dispatched branch); the next attempt
27	  builds that exact sha so every deterministic gate re-runs. Max 3 attempts /
28	  2 repairs, then fail loud. Repairs may never change the app version or touch
29	  `FEATURES.md` (`scripts/check-feature-markers.mjs` gates marker survival).
30	- **Nightly merge.** `.github/workflows/nightly-merge.yml` (02:13 UTC): when
31	  upstream publishes a newer `desktop-v*` tag, git merges it; Opus 5 resolves
32	  conflicted files, then a `(MERGE-ADAPT)` proactive port pass adapts fork-only
33	  callers to cleanly-merging upstream API refactors. Deterministic gates follow
34	  (FEATURES.md marker survival, dependency/lock consistency, `(REFERR-GATE)`
35	  cannot-find-name check), then a bounded `(MERGE-SEMANTIC-GATE)` review →
36	  adapt → fresh-review loop (max 3 reviews / 2 repairs). Green all the way =
37	  build (with its own repair loop), publish the Release, advance the baseline
38	  to the BUILT sha; ANY unrepaired failure hard-aborts with the baseline
39	  untouched → fix locally with the maintainer and re-baseline. A
40	  `rehearse=true` dispatch replays a night's merge half with zero side effects.
41	  A night blocked ONLY by a PROVEN `(AI-UNAVAILABLE)` abort (declared by the
42	  wrapper, never an exit code alone) merged, built and published nothing, so it
43	  concludes GREEN (no email) as a loud no-op with build/advance skipped — until
44	  `AI_UNAVAILABLE_STREAK_THRESHOLD` (7, owned by the script) consecutive blocked
45	  NIGHTS, which fails RED. Same-day re-runs count once, and only a night where
46	  the CLI provably reached the model clears the streak.
47	- **Key files.** `FEATURES.md` (feature manifest + fenced `markers` block the
48	  gates parse), `.fork/upstream-baseline.txt`,
49	  `scripts/check-dangerous-diagnostics.mjs` (REFERR gate),
50	  `scripts/check-feature-markers.mjs` (standalone marker gate),
51	  `scripts/check-no-bundled-skills.mjs` (blocks bundled Superset skills),
52	  `scripts/ci-repair.sh` (build-repair engine),
53	  `scripts/ai-run.sh` ((AI-UNAVAILABLE) classification + shared Claude CLI wrapper),
54	  `scripts/ai-streak.sh` ((AI-UNAVAILABLE) green no-op + consecutive-blocked-night
55	  escalation),
56	  `scripts/check-override-consistency.mjs`, `scripts/resolve-release-age.mjs`,
57	  companion native packages `github.com/khairm/libsql-windows-arm64` +
58	  `github.com/khairm/tokenizers-windows-arm64`.
59	
60	## Non-negotiables
61	
62	- **Whole feature set or fail loud** — every `FEATURES.md` marker survives a
63	  merge or the run aborts; never ship a partial fork.
64	- **v2-only, forever** — the v2 cloud/host-service stack is pinned on; never v1.
65	- **No bundled Superset skills** — never package or inject them; remove only
66	  marker-proven legacy copies. Keep hooks and user-owned skills.
67	- **No phone-home to upstream (phase 1)** — upstream's telemetry, auto-update
68	  and desktop-notice channels are deliberately SEVERED as of cloud severance
69	  phase 1 (`(CLOUD-SEVERANCE-P1)`, `(EGRESS-FENCE)`): dead PostHog/Sentry keys,
70	  a no-op CLI analytics call, a disabled updater and a notices poll that fetches
71	  nothing are the intended state, not breakage to repair. Sign-in, Electric and
72	  the api.superset.sh data plane are still live and are phase 2/3.
73	- **One version, ever** — exactly one Release per upstream version, tagged
74	  `desktop-v<version>`, rebuilt in place; no betas/prereleases.
75	- **No build-time type/test gate except `(REFERR-GATE)`** — the tree carries
76	  accepted type debt; only cannot-find-name diagnostics fail the build.
77	  Validate + e2e locally before relying on a release.
78	- **Everything is AI-touchable** (needs `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`): the nightly
79	  merge resolves/ports/reviews, and the build self-repairs via `(BUILD-REPAIR)`.
80	  Workflow YAML self-repair additionally needs the `WORKFLOW_PUSH_TOKEN` secret
81	  (fine-grained PAT, Contents+Workflows write) and only takes effect the NEXT
82	  run — workflow files are frozen once a run starts, which is why all step
83	  logic lives in `.github/actions/` + `scripts/` (repairable mid-run).
84	  Rate-limited/unparsable AI output aborts rather than ships.
85	
86	## Custom features / overrides
87	
88	`FEATURES.md` is the authoritative manifest (descriptions + marker tokens).
89	In brief:
90	
91	- **Native Windows ARM64 packaging** — one-click installer; ARM64 node-pty,
92	  libsql, tokenizers; renderer CORS for `superset-app://`.
93	- **Window controls** — native `titleBarOverlay` is the sole min/max/close on
94	  Windows, theme-matched; upstream's duplicates hidden.
95	- **Windows behaviour fixes** — skip quit-confirm; cmd.exe fallback;
96	  force-foreground; hidden-window watchdog; WebGL first-paint recovery; Wispr
97	  Flow accessibility/paste fix; fast non-blocking startup.
98	- **Agent status dots (Claude + Codex)** — per-terminal + workspace-rollup dot:
99	  red = needs input, yellow = working (incl. subagents/teammates/compaction/
100	  codex-companion holds), green = ready for review, blue = shell/background/
101	  cloud activity; precedence red > yellow > blue > green. All surfaces (tab,
102	  pane header, sidebar row + agent chips, rollup, kanban card) derive from one
103	  per-source primitive with independent latched axes; hook-driven via
104	  `superset-notify.py` POSTs with self-healing markers and persistence across
105	  renderer reloads; companion phone/watch alerts cover blocked questions,
106	  ready-for-review, and terminal-agent failures.
107	- **Auto-resume** — after an API failure, idle Claude terminals re-send
108	  automatically (bounded retries/budget, default-on, away-detection).
109	- **Recycle Bin** — every delete entry point soft-deletes (30-day display
110	  window); permanent delete only from inside the bin.
111	- **Exiting a card closes its runtime** — Completed, Archive, Snooze and Recycle
112	  Bin clear the workspace's tabs, dispose its terminals and release its pinned
113	  Claude account, for every card type and entry point. Worktree and branch
114	  untouched; a restored thread comes back empty. Snooze's account release is

333:## Internationalization
334-
335-User-facing strings use Lingui macros with the English text as the message id —
336-`<Trans>Text</Trans>` or `useLingui()`'s `t({ message })` in React, `i18n._(msg({ message }))`

338-so it translates separately. Numbers, currencies, and dates go through

340-locale. After adding or changing strings, run `bun run check:i18n` (CI enforces it): it
341-regenerates the catalogs and lists every untranslated message per locale. Write those
342-translations yourself into each `locales/<locale>/messages.po` and commit the catalogs with
343-the change — nothing on CI fills translations for you. Conventions: `packages/i18n/README.md`;

content.text:
`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

<result>## Verdict

**Symptom patch.** The five call sites are correct and complete as a point fix, but they are one of ten defects the same missing gate produced, and nothing stops the eleventh.

---

### 1. Root cause is the absent i18n gate, not the call sites

**file:** `.github/actions/arm64-build/action.yml` (gate block ends line 144) and `.github/workflows/nightly-merge.yml`
**summary:** Upstream ships this exact gate; the fork deletes it along with every upstream workflow and never re-adds it.

Upstream `ci.yml:118-119` runs `bun run --cwd packages/i18n check` (extract + `compile --strict`) with the comment "a dirty diff means someone forgot to run [it]". `(WORKFLOW-FORK-OWNED)` removes all upstream workflows, so the fork's three workflows never touch i18n. Grep across `.github/` and `scripts/` for `i18n|lingui|messages.po`: one hit, a doc comment.

Proof this is the real root cause, not a theory: `extract` surfaced **9** new messages, only **one** of which ("Kanban") came from the five converted sites. The other 8 were fork strings already written correctly as text-as-id that had simply never been extracted:

```
Archive workspace / Download Latest Release / Failed to open releases page: {message}
Failed to refresh changes / Preview notice: blocking (downgraded to a warning)
Runs in {masterLabel} / Terminal session did not close / The host will keep retrying.
```

Those shipped English-only in all 16 locales, silently. `--clean` also removed **51** stale entries (bundled-skills removal, severed updater, sign-in). Net churn ~180 lines per locale × 17. The catalogs have been drifting since the fork diverged; the dotted ids were just the only drift visible to a user.

**Cost of leaving it:** the next fork string repeats this. Worse, `(MERGE-ADAPT)` rewriting fork copy changes the derived id, stranding all 16 translations with no gate to notice.

### 2. What the gate should assert, and where

**Simplest, most general — recommended:** `scripts/check-lingui-explicit-ids.mjs`. Fail if any `Trans` / `t` / `msg` / `defineMessage` / `i18n._` descriptor carries an `id:` key. ~20 lines, no lingui CLI, seconds to run, zero translation burden, and it kills exactly the class that reached a user (raw token rendered in prod). Register beside `check-no-bundled-skills.mjs` in the build action, and add to `FROZEN_GATE_PATHS` at `scripts/ci-repair.sh:104`.

**Complete but expensive:** adopt upstream's step verbatim plus `git diff --exit-code packages/i18n/locales`. Catches the other 8 and the 51 stale entries. Three costs: `extract` runs babel over 14 source roots at `--workers 1` (minutes on the Windows ARM64 runner); it contradicts the "No build-time type/test gate except `(REFERR-GATE)`" non-negotiable, so it needs an AGENTS.md amendment or a home in nightly-merge's deterministic block instead; and once it is a build gate, `(BUILD-REPAIR)` can satisfy it by inventing 144 unreviewed translations and publishing them. If adopted, make it diagnosis-only for the repair agent.

### 3. Text-as-id is the right call for fork strings

**file:** `apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/formatResetTime/formatResetTime.ts:57`
**summary:** Correct convention; one accepted collision worth knowing about.

An explicit fork-only id is only safe if someone maintains the catalog, which is the thing that is not happening. Text-as-id degrades to readable English instead of a raw token, and it minimises merge delta. Also: line 8 of this same file *already* used `msg({ message: "now" })` — the two siblings were inconsistent, so this is convergence, not a new choice.

Trade accepted: `"now"` now shares one catalog entry with `pull-requests/$prNumber/page.tsx:545`, `marketing/.../ProgressSidebar.tsx:177`, and `web/.../SessionCard.tsx:18`. ja renders 今 for all four. Upstream already accepted that collapse for its own `"now"`, so matching it is right. `context:` in the descriptor is the escape hatch if the reset countdown reads wrong — do not go back to an id.

### 4. Nothing else in the tree can produce this failure today

Zero `<Trans id=`, zero `id:` inside any lingui descriptor (multiline AST-shaped grep), zero `i18n._("literal")`, zero `<Trans id={…}>`. All 16 non-source locales have **0** empty `msgstr`. `en` has 4926 msgids and matches extract. The point fix is complete.

### 5. Hand-translation is fine at this size; the fragility is that nothing verifies it

144 translations (9 × 16). Spot-checked de/ja/cs/vi: placeholders and ICU preserved, glossary honoured (vi keeps "workspace" English, matching its 515 existing uses; de uses "Arbeitsbereich"). `packages/i18n/test/catalog-integrity.test.ts` exists precisely to catch a dropped `{placeholder}` that `--strict` cannot see — **and the fork runs no tests in CI, so it has never run.** Same root cause, wider blast radius. The cheap answer is not translation tooling; it is `bun test --cwd packages/i18n` (5 files, deterministic, no network) wherever the gate lands.

### 6. Minor: AGENTS.md's i18n section is stale and misleads the merge agent

**file:** `AGENTS.md`, Internationalization section
**summary:** Two false statements that `(MERGE-ADAPT)` reads as ground truth.

It says "CI enforces it" (false in this fork) and cites `scripts/sort-po-references.ts` with `orderBy: "messageId"`. That file exists nowhere in the tree; `packages/i18n/lingui.config.ts:27` now uses `format: formatter({ origins: false })` and `orderBy: "message"`. **Cost:** one-line edits, but leaving them means every nightly agent believes a gate is protecting catalogs that nothing protects.</result>

**Symptom patch.** The five call sites are correct and complete as a point fix, but they are one of ten defects the same missing gate produced, and nothing stops the eleventh.

### 1. Root cause is the absent i18n gate, not the call sites

**file:** `.github/actions/arm64-build/action.yml` (gate block ends line 144) and `.github/workflows/nightly-merge.yml`
**summary:** Upstream ships this exact gate; the fork deletes it along with every upstream workflow and never re-adds it.

Upstream `ci.yml:118-119` runs `bun run --cwd packages/i18n check` (extract + `compile --strict`) with the comment "a dirty diff means someone forgot to run [it]". `(WORKFLOW-FORK-OWNED)` removes all upstream workflows, so the fork's three workflows never touch i18n. Grep across `.github/` and `scripts/` for `i18n|lingui|messages.po`: one hit, a doc comment.

Proof this is the real root cause, not a theory: `extract` surfaced **9** new messages, only **one** of which ("Kanban") came from the five converted sites. The other 8 were fork strings already written correctly as text-as-id that had simply never been extracted:

```
Archive workspace / Download Latest Release / Failed to open releases page: {message}
Failed to refresh changes / Preview notice: blocking (downgraded to a warning)
Runs in {masterLabel} / Terminal session did not close / The host will keep retrying.
```

Those shipped English-only in all 16 locales, silently. `--clean` also removed **51** stale entries (bundled-skills removal, severed updater, sign-in). Net churn ~180 lines per locale × 17. The catalogs have been drifting since the fork diverged; the dotted ids were just the only drift visible to a user.

**Cost of leaving it:** the next fork string repeats this. Worse, `(MERGE-ADAPT)` rewriting fork copy changes the derived id, stranding all 16 translations with no gate to notice.

### 2. What the gate should assert, and where

**Simplest, most general — recommended:** `scripts/check-lingui-explicit-ids.mjs`. Fail if any `Trans` / `t` / `msg` / `defineMessage` / `i18n._` descriptor carries an `id:` key. ~20 lines, no lingui CLI, seconds to run, zero translation burden, and it kills exactly the class that reached a user (raw token rendered in prod). Register beside `check-no-bundled-skills.mjs` in the build action, and add to `FROZEN_GATE_PATHS` at `scripts/ci-repair.sh:104`.

**Complete but expensive:** adopt upstream's step verbatim plus `git diff --exit-code packages/i18n/locales`. Catches the other 8 and the 51 stale entries. Three costs: `extract` runs babel over 14 source roots at `--workers 1` (minutes on the Windows ARM64 runner); it contradicts the "No build-time type/test gate except `(REFERR-GATE)`" non-negotiable, so it needs an AGENTS.md amendment or a home in nightly-merge's deterministic block instead; and once it is a build gate, `(BUILD-REPAIR)` can satisfy it by inventing 144 unreviewed translations and publishing them. If adopted, make it diagnosis-only for the repair agent.

### 3. Text-as-id is the right call for fork strings

**file:** `apps/desktop/src/renderer/lib/formatResetTime/formatResetTime.ts:57`
**summary:** Correct convention; one accepted collision worth knowing about.

An explicit fork-only id is only safe if someone maintains the catalog, which is the thing that is not happening. Text-as-id degrades to readable English instead of a raw token, and it minimises merge delta. Also: line 8 of this same file *already* used `msg({ message: "now" })` — the two siblings were inconsistent, so this is convergence, not a new choice.

Trade accepted: `"now"` now shares one catalog entry with `pull-requests/$prNumber/page.tsx:545`, `marketing/.../ProgressSidebar.tsx:177`, and `web/.../SessionCard.tsx:18`. ja renders 今 for all four. Upstream already accepted that collapse for its own `"now"`, so matching it is right. `context:` in the descriptor is the escape hatch if the reset countdown reads wrong — do not go back to an id.

### 4. Nothing else in the tree can produce this failure today

Zero `<Trans id=`, zero `id:` inside any lingui descriptor (multiline AST-shaped grep), zero `i18n._("literal")`, zero `<Trans id={…}>`. All 16 non-source locales have **0** empty `msgstr`. `en` has 4926 msgids and matches extract. The point fix is complete.

### 5. Hand-translation is fine at this size; the fragility is that nothing verifies it

144 translations (9 × 16). Spot-checked de/ja/cs/vi: placeholders and ICU preserved, glossary honoured (vi keeps "workspace" English, matching its 515 existing uses; de uses "Arbeitsbereich"). `packages/i18n/test/catalog-integrity.test.ts` exists precisely to catch a dropped `{placeholder}` that `--strict` cannot see — **and the fork runs no tests in CI, so it has never run.** Same root cause, wider blast radius. The cheap answer is not translation tooling; it is `bun test --cwd packages/i18n` (5 files, deterministic, no network) wherever the gate lands.

### 6. Minor: AGENTS.md's i18n section is stale and misleads the merge agent

**file:** `AGENTS.md`, Internationalization section
**summary:** Two false statements that `(MERGE-ADAPT)` reads as ground truth.

It says "CI enforces it" (false in this fork) and cites `scripts/sort-po-references.ts` with `orderBy: "messageId"`. That file exists nowhere in the tree; `packages/i18n/lingui.config.ts:27` now uses `format: formatter({ origins: false })` and `orderBy: "message"`. **Cost:** one-line edits, but leaving them means every nightly agent believes a gate is protecting catalogs that nothing protects.</result>

85:| ReferenceError-class build gate | the build (and therefore every nightly, whose build job calls the same workflow) fails on cannot-find-name tsc diagnostics ONLY (TS2304/2552/2662/2663/18004) — bare identifiers esbuild bundles fine but that throw ReferenceError at runtime, exactly what a CLEAN-merging upstream hunk can leave in fork code the AI resolver never sees (v1.14.0 layout.tsx incident: upstream renamed the workspace source variable in a non-conflicting hunk; fork's cache-first hold kept referencing it; every v2 workspace view crashed). Per-package direct tsc (turbo graph is debt-blocked); the accepted type debt has zero of these codes so the gate can't false-abort | `(REFERR-GATE)` |
109:| Cloud severance phase 1 (telemetry / update / notices) | this fork does not phone home. FOUR channels are cut at once and each is enforced at build time, not by configuration a merge can flip back. (1) **Telemetry keys are BANNED**: `assertNoTelemetryKeys` runs immediately after the repo-root `.env` load in `electron.vite.config.ts` and THROWS if `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY`, `SENTRY_DSN_DESKTOP`, `SENTRY_DSN_HOST_SERVICE` or `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` is set — a throw rather than a silent force-empty, because quietly rewriting a value the maintainer put in `.env` hides the disagreement instead of surfacing it. Banning `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` also disarms the two build-time sourcemap-UPLOAD plugins, themselves a phone-home to upstream's Sentry org. A `.env` carrying ports/URLs/workspace name keeps working. name: ARM64 build steps
description: >
  All build/package/verify steps for the Windows ARM64 installer. Publishing is
  deliberately NOT here: it lives in .github/workflows/build-arm64.yml, after
  the frozen pre-publish release gates, so a repaired build cannot ship a
  Release before those gates have passed.
  Lives under .github/actions (NOT .github/workflows) deliberately: this file
  is part of the checked-out tree, so the (BUILD-REPAIR) AI loop can fix it
  mid-run and the next attempt picks the fix up — workflow YAML is frozen once
  a run starts and GITHUB_TOKEN cannot push it. Keep every step here a thin
  shim over scripts/ where possible.
inputs:
  gh-token:
    description: token for gh release download/create + tag push
    required: true

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Read app version
      shell: bash
      run: |
        V=$(node -p "require('./apps/desktop/package.json').version")
        [ -n "$V" ] || { echo "::error::could not read apps/desktop/package.json version"; exit 1; }
        echo "App version: $V"

    - name: Setup Node.js
      uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version: '22'

    - name: Setup Bun (native Windows ARM64)
      uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
      with:
        # 1.3.14 = last stable Zig release; first native win-arm64 shipped in 1.3.10.
        bun-version: '1.3.14'

    - name: Verify Bun is native ARM64 (fail fast, fall back to official zip)
      shell: pwsh
      run: ./scripts/verify-bun-arm64.ps1

    - name: Install dependencies (frozen lockfile)
      shell: bash
      env:
        # Skip the flaky @electron/rebuild postinstall (install:deps). On
        # win-arm64 it can't build native trustedDeps; the deterministic
        # Bun-store payload repair (materialize-native-closure) handles them.
        SUPERSET_POSTINSTALL_RUNNING: '1'
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        # The committed bun.lock is the source of truth and is consistent with
        # our pinned package.json (node-pty @lydell alias, mastra pins), so a
        # FROZEN install uses the locked versions and never re-resolves — which
        # also sidesteps bunfig's minimumReleaseAge gate (locked versions are
        # not age-checked). If this fails the lock drifted from package.json:
        # regenerate it (bun install --lockfile-only) and recommit.
        bun install --frozen-lockfile

    # (REFERR-GATE) Fail on cannot-find-name diagnostics ONLY (TS2304/2552/
    # 2662/2663/18004) — bare identifiers esbuild bundles fine but that throw
    # ReferenceError at runtime. NOT a full type gate: the tree's known type
    # debt has zero of these codes and stays allowed.
    - name: ReferenceError-class typecheck gate
      shell: bash
      run: node scripts/check-dangerous-diagnostics.mjs

    - name: Generate file icons
      shell: bash
      working-directory: apps/desktop
      run: bun run generate:icons

    - name: Build app (electron-vite / esbuild)
      shell: bash
      working-directory: apps/desktop
      run: bun run compile:app

    - name: Verify renderer bundle guards (screenReaderMode)
      shell: bash
      working-directory: apps/desktop
      run: bash ../../scripts/verify-renderer-guards.sh

    - name: Fetch native prebuilds + materialize win-arm64 closure
      shell: bash
      env:
        GH_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.gh-token }}
      run: bash scripts/fetch-native-prebuilds.sh

    - name: Prepare native modules (ARM64 target)
      shell: bash
      working-directory: apps/desktop
      env:
        TARGET_ARCH: arm64
        TARGET_PLATFORM: win32
      run: bun run copy:native-modules

    - name: Validate native runtime (ARM64 fail-fast gate)
      shell: bash
      env:
        TARGET_ARCH: arm64
        TARGET_PLATFORM: win32
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        bash scripts/materialize-native-closure.sh
        cd apps/desktop
        bun run validate:native-runtime

    - name: Build Windows ARM64 installer
      shell: bash
      working-directory: apps/desktop
      env:
        CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY: 'false'
        # native-keymap etc. use V8 APIs Electron 40 deprecated; MSVC C4996
        # under warnings-as-errors fails node-gyp. /wd4996 disables just that
        # warning for all native rebuilds (deterministic; runtime is fine).
        CL: '/wd4996'
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        npx electron-builder --win --arm64 --publish never --config electron-builder.ts
        echo "--- release dir ---"
        ls -la release || true

    - name: Verify packaged native closure (ARM64 fail-fast gate)
      shell: bash
      working-directory: apps/desktop
      run: bash ../../scripts/verify-packaged-natives.sh

    # (CLOUD-SEVERANCE-P1) Runs LAST of the verify steps: it is the only gate
    # that needs both the compiled bundles (dist/) and the packaged output
    # (release/, for app-update.yml). Deliberately invoked WITHOUT
    # --no-artifacts — that flag is for local source-only runs, and in CI the
    # artifact assertions are the point.
    #
    # This copy is for FAST FEEDBACK only. The step that actually decides is
    # "Enforce pre-publish release gates" in .github/workflows/build-arm64.yml,
    # which is frozen for the whole run and out of reach of a mid-run repair —
    # and which runs BEFORE the release is published. Publishing deliberately
    # no longer lives in this composite action for exactly that reason.
    - name: Verify no bundled Superset skills
      shell: bash
      run: node scripts/check-no-bundled-skills.mjs

    - name: Verify cloud severance (telemetry / update channels)
      shell: bash
      run: node scripts/check-cloud-severance.mjs

| Agent status dots (Claude + Codex) | per-terminal dot + workspace rollup; host-service POST + JSONL watcher | `pane-map-hook`, `StatusIndicator` |
| Claude account Pi outage grace | suppress the outage toast and accept queued sidebar switches for the first 10 continuous minutes; keep old credentials during that grace, then fail loud if the switch still cannot complete | `(CLAUDE-ACCOUNT-PI-GRACE)` |
| No bundled Superset skills | never package or inject upstream Superset skills; remove only marker-proven legacy copies | `(NO-BUNDLED-SKILLS)` |
| Companion lifecycle alerts | phone + custom watch receive distinct ready-for-review and terminal-agent-failure notifications; ready fires once per real work cycle after a 10s continuous-green settle window, tool/subagent/admin failures are excluded, and presence/sidebar curation match blocked-agent push behavior | `(COMPANION-LIFECYCLE-ALERTS)` |
| Companion alerts name their chat | every phone/watch alert — ready (`g`), agent-error (`e`) and blocked-question — says WHICH chat it is about: title `<project> · <workspace>`, body `<tab> — <event text>`, with the tab named only when the workspace has 2+ tabs and a title resolved. The three names ride the FCM push as PLAINTEXT under an explicit owner waiver recorded 2026-08-16 ("i dont care if google sees it", re-confirmed via AskUser) — and ONLY those three: question text, option text, file paths, branch names and every other free string stay banned, the exempt key set `{pn,wn,tn}` is enumerated by a test, and v1/v2 keep their 160-byte leak tripwire while only v3 gets 2048. Wire schema v3 is closed PER (VERSION, KIND) — `q`=[v,k,i,w,n,x,t,pn,wn,tn,tc], `g`=[v,k,i,w,x,gx,t,pn,wn,tn,tc], `e`=[v,k,i,w,x,t,pn,wn,tn,tc], `c`=[v,k,i,w,x,gx,t] — with EVERY key always present and `""` spelling absence, because the phone's parser is exact-equality in both directions and a missing key would silence the alert rather than degrade it; the host mirrors the phone's golden vectors byte-for-byte in its own suite. `g` and `e` deliberately no longer share a key set: a ready alert must carry `gx` (13 digits, the OUTCOME event's instant — the same one the alert id hashes, never anything send-shaped, since presence gating can send an earlier finish later) and a non-empty `t` (the terminal handle, read off the ALERT ROW rather than the nullable context resolver, because it is the notification's identity on the phone and a failed context lookup may cost names but never identity), while an error alert carries neither and an `e` smuggling `gx` throws. Names are sanitised TOTALLY (never throws: controls/C1/U+2028/U+2029/newlines stripped, 256-byte UTF-8 budget, truncation walked by CODE POINT so an emoji can never be cut into a lone surrogate) and resolved INSIDE the send — fresh on every retry, never cached on a held alert — so a workspace renamed mid-hold buzzes with its new name, and a resolver that throws costs the names, never the notification. Tab titles live only in the renderer, so a per-workspace snapshot (`pane.kind==="terminal"` + `pane.data.terminalId`, title precedence tab rename > pane rename > live terminal title > nothing, one terminal in two differently-named tabs ⇒ no tab name) is pushed over two new PROTECTED tRPC mutations and held in a bounded process-local registry that re-derives every workspace↔terminal relationship from `host.db` before an atomic replace. Lifecycle alerts now RETRACT — deliberately overriding the old "lifecycle alerts are not retracted" invariant rather than layering over it: reading the chat on the desktop (focus-clear or sidebar mark-read, and ONLY when a green dot was actually removed — never the resync's cold-start seeding, which would mass-retract on every launch) or the SESSION ENDING sends a v3 `c`, and alert ids are hashed from the FINAL outcome event's instant so `markLifecycleSeen` can recompute one after a host restart with no schema change. A DELIVERED READY CARD COMES DOWN THE MOMENT THE TERMINAL STOPS BEING READY, whatever ends it: a new work cycle, a status that proves the agent is working or blocked again, a session end, a dead terminal, a relaunch, a curated-off thread or a read. It used to have one exception — a card overtaken by a NEW WORK CYCLE was retired SILENTLY and left on the handset for the next `g` to replace in place, to bound the noise measured overnight on v0.1.0 (one chat finished sixteen times ~15 minutes apart while the user was away and stacked sixteen buzzing notifications for a single unread conversation). The argument held only while a next `g` actually arrived: when the agent went back to work and then blocked, crashed or was left alone, nothing replaced the card and the phone said "ready for review" for six hours about a chat that was not. USER DECISION, reversing it: retract immediately and let the companion app absorb the higher event rate. Each alert is still owed EXACTLY ONE `c`, carrying that alert's own `gx` so the phone cancels the finish it is actually holding rather than whatever card is showing; a retracted row is kept to its TTL as the cycle's dedupe record, so repeats — twenty further cycles, a session end behind a new cycle, two retirements over one in-flight send — are inert rather than a second broadcast. Because the green dot is cleared by the agent starting work again while a card may still be on the phone, the desktop also keeps a per-terminal OUTSTANDING-READY record beside its seen marks: opening a chat that is already running again reports a read for the finish that record names, the record is retired only when a host actually APPLIED the report AND only up to the generation that host acknowledged (a newer finish landing mid-report keeps its own record; a host that refused the read on its own evidence — host.db does not place that terminal in that workspace, or could not be read to check — answers `accepted: false` so the record survives for the resync to offer again), and the resync repairs the ones that were dropped — under the same cap, rotation and cooldowns as the existing repair, and never inventing one out of its own replay. Generations are ordered by a per-terminal MONOTONIC lifecycle instant (`max(now, previous+1)`, anchored on the persisted binding so it survives a restart) rather than the raw wall clock, because an NTP step-back would otherwise stamp a newer finish behind its predecessor — which the phone rejects as stale, the host cannot retract, and the renderer records as reported. And a read is bounded by its OWN instant: `markLifecycleSeen` retires every generation at or before `seenThroughAt` and leaves later ones alone, so a delayed or resync-replayed read of an earlier finish can never retract work the user has not seen. Its "nothing ever existed, so send nothing" branch is bounded the same way — per terminal, against the last lifecycle instant host.db recorded before the manager started (read once at bridge start), because a wall-clock start compared against a monotonic generation lets a restart inside a backstep "prove" that an alert the previous process actually sent never existed; unreadable or absent restart evidence disables the proof rather than trusting it, since a blind `c` the phone drops is the safe failure and a swallowed retraction is not. Every other retirement still fires its `c` — a session end (the chat is gone, so tapping it would open nothing) and a read (the event that resets the cycle) — and `e` alerts are excluded from the rule entirely, because an agent that died is not superseded by later work and an unseen error must not be quietly folded away. Retract sends (v1 `r` AND v3 `c`) now use the 24 h `RETRACT_TTL_MS` as the FCM envelope TTL, closing a latent gap where a handset off the network for 15 minutes kept a notification for an answered question | `(ALERT-CONTEXT-NAMES)` |
...
| Idle teammates green deterministically | Claude Code reports finished teammates in the Stop payload's background_tasks[] as `status:"running"` FOREVER (captured live: 33 teammate entries, all "runni
| ReferenceError-class build gate | the build (and therefore every nightly, whose build job calls the same workflow) fails on cannot-find-name tsc diagnostics ONLY (TS2304/2552/2662/2663/18004) — ba
| Nightly dependency-consistency + lock regen | the nightly merge can introduce dependency-state drift that only the build discovers (after a windows-arm64 runner spins up): a stale fork root `overrid

"`packages/i18n/locales/en/messages.po` renders as the RAW ID in the packaged app — the babel macro strips the "
"inline fallback in a production build, which is how the sidebar shipped the literal text "
"`dashboard.sidebar.header.kanban` instead of \"Kanban\" for four releases. Upstream's CI catches this by "
"re-running `lingui extract` + `compile --strict` and failing on a dirty catalog diff; `(WORKFLOW-FORK-OWNED)` "
"drops every upstream workflow, so nothing caught it here. The gate asserts the narrower, source-only invariant "
"— every explicit lingui id in the source resolves in the English catalog — over the same roots and exclusions "
"`lingui.config.ts` extracts from, with no lingui CLI and no babel pass. Text-as-id call sites "
"(`<Trans>Kanban</Trans>`, `t({ message })`), the convention this repo now follows, are deliberately unchecked: "
"a missed extract there degrades to readable English, not to a visible token. A FULL extract-and-diff gate was "
"rejected twice over — babel over 14 source roots costs minutes on the ARM64 runner, and once a catalog diff is "
"a build gate `(BUILD-REPAIR)` can satisfy it by inventing 144 unreviewed translations and publishing them | "
"`(I18N-ID-GATE)` |\n")

lines = s.split("\n")
for i, line in enumerate(lines):
    if line.startswith("| ReferenceError-class build gate |"):
        lines.insert(i + 1, row.rstrip("\n"))
        break
else:
    raise SystemExit("anchor row not found")

for i, line in enumerate(lines):
    if line.startswith("(REFERR-GATE)\t"):
        lines.insert(i + 1, "(I18N-ID-GATE)\tscripts/check-lingui-explicit-ids.mjs")
        break
else:
    raise SystemExit("anchor marker not found")

io.open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="").write("\n".join(lines))
print("ok")

name: ARM64 build steps
description: >
  All build/package/verify steps for the Windows ARM64 installer. Publishing is
  deliberately NOT here: it lives in .github/workflows/build-arm64.yml, after
  the frozen pre-publish release gates, so a repaired build cannot ship a
  Release before those gates have passed.
  Lives under .github/actions (NOT .github/workflows) deliberately: this file
  is part of the checked-out tree, so the (BUILD-REPAIR) AI loop can fix it
  mid-run and the next attempt picks the fix up — workflow YAML is frozen once
  a run starts and GITHUB_TOKEN cannot push it. Keep every step here a thin
  shim over scripts/ where possible.
inputs:
  gh-token:
    description: token for gh release download/create + tag push
    required: true

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Read app version
      shell: bash
      run: |
        V=$(node -p "require('./apps/desktop/package.json').version")
        [ -n "$V" ] || { echo "::error::could not read apps/desktop/package.json version"; exit 1; }
        echo "App version: $V"

    - name: Setup Node.js
      uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version: '22'

    - name: Setup Bun (native Windows ARM64)
      uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
      with:
        # 1.3.14 = last stable Zig release; first native win-arm64 shipped in 1.3.10.
        bun-version: '1.3.14'

    - name: Verify Bun is native ARM64 (fail fast, fall back to official zip)
      shell: pwsh
      run: ./scripts/verify-bun-arm64.ps1

    - name: Install dependencies (frozen lockfile)
      shell: bash
      env:
        # Skip the flaky @electron/rebuild postinstall (install:deps). On
        # win-arm64 it can't build native trustedDeps; the deterministic
        # Bun-store payload repair (materialize-native-closure) handles them.
        SUPERSET_POSTINSTALL_RUNNING: '1'
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        # The committed bun.lock is the source of truth and is consistent with
        # our pinned package.json (node-pty @lydell alias, mastra pins), so a
        # FROZEN install uses the locked versions and never re-resolves — which
        # also sidesteps bunfig's minimumReleaseAge gate (locked versions are
        # not age-checked). If this fails the lock drifted from package.json:
        # regenerate it (bun install --lockfile-only) and recommit.
        bun install --frozen-lockfile

    # (REFERR-GATE) Fail on cannot-find-name diagnostics ONLY (TS2304/2552/
    # 2662/2663/18004) — bare identifiers esbuild bundles fine but that throw

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# (I18N-CATALOG-GATE) Proves the committed Lingui catalogs are exactly what the
# current source extracts to.
#
# Why the obvious cheap check does not work: at upstream 1.26.0 the English
# source text IS the message id, and the production Babel macro resolves
# `descriptorFields: "auto"` to `"id-only"` — it strips the inline fallback and
# emits only a hashed id. A string missing from the catalog therefore renders as
# `OGXtL8`, not as English. Nothing short of running extraction can tell whether
# a call site made it into the catalog, so this gate runs the real thing.
#
# It is the check upstream's own CI runs and that (WORKFLOW-FORK-OWNED) dropped
# along with every upstream workflow — which is how the sidebar shipped the
# literal text `dashboard.sidebar.header.kanban` instead of "Kanban".
#
# Failure means someone changed user-facing copy without regenerating the
# catalogs, OR a merge left a catalog stale. Both are fixed the same way, by a
# human: `bun run check:i18n`, translate anything new, commit the catalogs.
#
# DELIBERATELY NOT self-repairable ((BUILD-REPAIR) cannot reach a frozen
# workflow step, and this script is frozen in ci-repair.sh): the only way to
# satisfy a dirty-catalog failure is to write translations, and unreviewed
# machine-invented translations in sixteen languages is exactly what must not
# ship unattended.
set -euo pipefail

if [ ! -f package.json ]; then
	echo "::error::(I18N-CATALOG-GATE) run from the repository root; package.json is missing"
	exit 1
fi

if ! git diff --quiet -- packages/i18n/locales ||
	[ -n "$(git status --porcelain -- packages/i18n/locales)" ]; then
	echo "::error::(I18N-CATALOG-GATE) packages/i18n/locales is already dirty before extraction; refusing to run so the result cannot be attributed to this gate"
	git status --porcelain -- packages/i18n/locales
	exit 1
fi

echo "(I18N-CATALOG-GATE) regenerating catalogs from source"
bun run --cwd packages/i18n extract
bun run --cwd packages/i18n compile

if ! git diff --quiet -- packages/i18n/locales ||
	[ -n "$(git status --porcelain -- packages/i18n/locales)" ]; then
	echo "::error::(I18N-CATALOG-GATE) the committed catalogs do not match what the source extracts to. A message missing from the catalog renders as its hashed id (e.g. OGXtL8) in a production build. Run 'bun run check:i18n', fill in any new translations, and commit packages/i18n/locales."
	git --no-pager diff --stat -- packages/i18n/locales
	git --no-pager diff -- packages/i18n/locales | head -n 200
	exit 1
fi

echo "(I18N-CATALOG-GATE) catalogs match the source"

p = ".github/workflows/build-arm64.yml"
s = io.open(p, encoding="utf-8", newline="").read()

step = """      # (I18N-CATALOG-GATE) THE catalog enforcement point, in the WORKFLOW for
      # the same reason as the severance gate below: a mid-run (BUILD-REPAIR)
      # agent can rewrite .github/actions/** and scripts/**, but not this file.
      # Freezing only the script would have been theatre — a repair could have
      # deleted its invocation and left the frozen script sitting unused.
      #
      # Regenerating the catalogs is the ONLY check that works here. At 1.26.0
      # the English text is the message id and the production macro emits
      # id-only, so a call site missing from the catalog renders as a hashed id
      # (OGXtL8), not as English: no source-only scan can see that.
      #
      # Threat model, stated rather than implied: this is drift detection, not
      # tamper-proofing. It deliberately does NOT pin PATH the way the severance
      # step does, because it needs the bun the setup step put there. A repair
      # that shadows `bun` defeats it; a repair that forgets to regenerate
      # catalogs does not, and that is the failure this exists for.
      - name: Enforce i18n catalog consistency (frozen — cannot be repaired away)
        shell: bash
        env:
          BASH_ENV: ''
          ENV: ''
          NODE_OPTIONS: ''
          NODE_PATH: ''
        run: bash scripts/check-i18n-catalogs.sh

""".replace("\n", eol)

count = s.count(anchor)
assert count == 3, f"expected 3 severance anchors, found {count}"
io.open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="").write(s.replace(anchor, step + anchor))

row = ("| i18n catalog build gate | a user-facing string missing from `packages/i18n/locales` renders as a HASHED ID "
"(`OGXtL8`) in the packaged app, never as English: at upstream 1.26.0 the English text IS the message id and the "
"production Babel macro resolves `descriptorFields: \"auto\"` to `id-only`, stripping the inline fallback. That is how "
"the sidebar shipped the literal text `dashboard.sidebar.header.kanban` for four releases, and how eight other "
"fork-only strings shipped English-only in all sixteen locales. Upstream's CI catches it by regenerating the catalogs "
"and failing on a dirty diff; `(WORKFLOW-FORK-OWNED)` drops every upstream workflow, so nothing caught it here. "
"A CHEAPER SOURCE-ONLY GATE WAS BUILT FIRST AND THROWN AWAY, and the reason is the load-bearing part: it asserted only "
"that EXPLICIT dotted ids resolve in the English catalog, on the false premise that text-as-id call sites degrade to "
"readable English. They do not — they degrade to the hash — so the gate ignored the dominant case while passing green. "
"Nothing short of running extraction can tell whether a call site reached the catalog. The gate therefore regenerates "
"(`extract --clean --overwrite` + `compile --strict`) and fails on any diff under `packages/i18n/locales`, refusing to "
"run at all if that tree is already dirty so a pre-existing edit cannot be attributed to it. It is invoked from "
"`.github/workflows/build-arm64.yml` — the WORKFLOW, frozen for the whole run — in all three build attempts, not from "
"the repairable composite action, because freezing the script while leaving its invocation editable is theatre: a "
"repair would simply delete the step. The composite action keeps a copy for fast feedback. DELIBERATELY NOT "
"self-repairable: the only way to satisfy a dirty-catalog failure is to write translations, and unreviewed "
"machine-invented copy in sixteen languages is exactly what must not ship unattended. Stated threat-model limit: this "
"is drift detection, not tamper-proofing — unlike the severance step it does not pin PATH, because it needs the bun "
"the setup step provides, so a repair that shadows `bun` defeats it while a repair that forgets to regenerate does not | "
"`(I18N-CATALOG-GATE)` |")

out = []
for line in lines:
    if line.startswith("| Lingui message-id build gate |"):
        out.append(row)
    elif line.startswith("(I18N-ID-GATE)\t"):
        out.append("(I18N-CATALOG-GATE)\tscripts/check-i18n-catalogs.sh")
        out.append("(I18N-CATALOG-GATE)\t.github/workflows/build-arm64.yml")
    else:
        out.append(line)

assert any(l.startswith("| i18n catalog build gate |") for l in out), "row not replaced"
assert any(l.startswith("(I18N-CATALOG-GATE)\t") for l in out), "marker not replaced"
io.open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="").write(eol.join(out))
print("ok")

already follow) and `settings.usage.resetIn.now` in formatResetTime,
whose own sibling function already said `msg({ message: "now" })`. Both
reset-time call sites take `context: "countdown"`: the shared "now"
entry carries past-tense "just now" in fr/ko/vi/zh (à l'instant, 방금,
vừa xong, 刚刚), which reads as "a moment ago" for a reset due now.

Catalogs: `extract --clean` + `compile --strict`. Ten messages added,
nine of which were fork strings already written to convention and simply
never extracted — they had been shipping English-only in all sixteen
locales. 51 dead entries removed (severed updater, sign-in, bundled
skills, chat v3); each verified to have no live lingui call site.
Translations written by hand for all sixteen locales.

usePaneRegistry wrapped the identical strings in `t()`, and the tray and
app-menu "Download Latest Release" entries carried a comment claiming no
catalog could translate them, which the palette entry made false.

packages/i18n/locales. This is upstream's own check, dropped here with

degrade to readable English, which is false — they degrade to the hash —
so it ignored the dominant case while passing green. The invocation

toolUseResult.originalFile:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# (I18N-CATALOG-GATE) Proves the committed Lingui catalogs are exactly what the
# current source extracts to.
#
# Why the obvious cheap check does not work: at upstream 1.26.0 the English
# source text IS the message id, and the production Babel macro resolves
# `descriptorFields: "auto"` to `"id-only"` — it strips the inline fallback and
# emits only a hashed id. A string missing from the catalog therefore renders as
# `OGXtL8`, not as English. Nothing short of running extraction can tell whether
# a call site made it into the catalog, so this gate runs the real thing.
#
# It is the check upstream's own CI runs and that (WORKFLOW-FORK-OWNED) dropped
# along with every upstream workflow — which is how the sidebar shipped the
# literal text `dashboard.sidebar.header.kanban` instead of "Kanban".
#
# Failure means someone changed user-facing copy without regenerating the
# catalogs, OR a merge left a catalog stale. Both are fixed the same way, by a
# human: `bun run check:i18n`, translate anything new, commit the catalogs.
#
# DELIBERATELY NOT self-repairable ((BUILD-REPAIR) cannot reach a frozen
# workflow step, and this script is frozen in ci-repair.sh): the only way to
# satisfy a dirty-catalog failure is to write translations, and unreviewed
# machine-invented translations in sixteen languages is exactly what must not
# ship unattended.
set -euo pipefail

if [ ! -f package.json ]; then
	echo "::error::(I18N-CATALOG-GATE) run from the repository root; package.json is missing"
	exit 1
fi

if ! git diff --quiet -- packages/i18n/locales ||
	[ -n "$(git status --porcelain -- packages/i18n/locales)" ]; then
	echo "::error::(I18N-CATALOG-GATE) packages/i18n/locales is already dirty before extraction; refusing to run so the result cannot be attributed to this gate"
	git status --porcelain -- packages/i18n/locales
	exit 1
fi

echo "(I18N-CATALOG-GATE) regenerating catalogs from source"
bun run --cwd packages/i18n extract
bun run --cwd packages/i18n compile

if ! git diff --quiet -- packages/i18n/locales ||
	[ -n "$(git status --porcelain -- packages/i18n/locales)" ]; then
	echo "::error::(I18N-CATALOG-GATE) the committed catalogs do not match what the source extracts to. A message missing from the catalog renders as its hashed id (e.g. OGXtL8) in a production build. Run 'bun run check:i18n', fill in any new translations, and commit packages/i18n/locales."
	git --no-pager diff --stat -- packages/i18n/locales
	git --no-pager diff -- packages/i18n/locales | head -n 200
	exit 1
fi

echo "(I18N-CATALOG-GATE) catalogs match the source"

echo "(I18N-CATALOG-GATE) regenerating catalogs from source"
# The package's own `extract`/`compile` scripts shell out through
# `bunx --bun lingui`, which on Windows mis-parses a checkout path containing a

LINGUI="node_modules/.bin/lingui"
if [ ! -e "packages/i18n/$LINGUI" ]; then
	echo "::error::(I18N-CATALOG-GATE) packages/i18n/$LINGUI is missing; run 'bun install' first"
	exit 1
fi
# cd, not --config: lingui resolves <rootDir> from the config it DISCOVERS by
# walking up from the cwd, and the repo root carries a re-export of this config
# for the babel macro. Running from the root therefore resolves <rootDir> to the
# root, extracts nothing, writes a stray ./locales, and leaves the real
# catalogs untouched — a gate that passes green having checked nothing.
(cd packages/i18n && "$LINGUI" extract --clean --overwrite --workers 1)
(cd packages/i18n && "$LINGUI" compile --strict --workers 1)

# Fail loud on that exact silent-pass shape rather than trusting the cd above:
# a clean diff is only evidence if extraction actually collected the catalog.
MESSAGES=$(grep -c '^msgid ' packages/i18n/locales/en/messages.po || true)
if [ "$MESSAGES" -lt 1000 ]; then
	echo "::error::(I18N-CATALOG-GATE) extraction produced $MESSAGES messages in packages/i18n/locales/en/messages.po, far below the floor of 1000. Extraction did not see the source; a clean diff here would mean nothing."
	exit 1
fi
if [ -e locales ]; then
	echo "::error::(I18N-CATALOG-GATE) extraction wrote a stray ./locales at the repository root, which means it resolved the wrong config. Refusing to report a result."
	exit 1
fi

toolUseResult.originalFile:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# (I18N-CATALOG-GATE) Proves the committed Lingui catalogs are exactly what the
# current source extracts to.
#
# Why the obvious cheap check does not work: at upstream 1.26.0 the English
# source text IS the message id, and the production Babel macro resolves
# `descriptorFields: "auto"` to `"id-only"` — it strips the inline fallback and
# emits only a hashed id. A string missing from the catalog therefore renders as
# `OGXtL8`, not as English. Nothing short of running extraction can tell whether
# a call site made it into the catalog, so this gate runs the real thing.
#
# It is the check upstream's own CI runs and that (WORKFLOW-FORK-OWNED) dropped
# along with every upstream workflow — which is how the sidebar shipped the
# literal text `dashboard.sidebar.header.kanban` instead of "Kanban".
#
# Failure means someone changed user-facing copy without regenerating the
# catalogs, OR a merge left a catalog stale. Both are fixed the same way, by a
# human: `bun run check:i18n`, translate anything new, commit the catalogs.
#
# DELIBERATELY NOT self-repairable ((BUILD-REPAIR) cannot reach a frozen
# workflow step, and this script is frozen in ci-repair.sh): the only way to
# satisfy a dirty-catalog failure is to write translations, and unreviewed
# machine-invented translations in sixteen languages is exactly what must not
# ship unattended.
set -euo pipefail

if [ ! -f package.json ]; then
	echo "::error::(I18N-CATALOG-GATE) run from the repository root; package.json is missing"
	exit 1
fi

if ! git diff --quiet -- packages/i18n/locales ||
	[ -n "$(git status --porcelain -- packages/i18n/locales)" ]; then
	echo "::error::(I18N-CATALOG-GATE) packages/i18n/locales is already dirty before extraction; refusing to run so the result cannot be attributed to this gate"
	git status --porcelain -- packages/i18n/locales
	exit 1
fi

echo "(I18N-CATALOG-GATE) regenerating catalogs from source"
# The package's own `extract`/`compile` scripts shell out through
# `bunx --bun lingui`, which on Windows mis-parses a checkout path containing a
# space as a git remote and fails to resolve. The gate calls the installed
# binary directly so it behaves the same on a maintainer's machine and on the
# runner.
LINGUI="packages/i18n/node_modules/.bin/lingui"
if [ ! -x "$LINGUI" ] && [ ! -f "$LINGUI" ]; then
	echo "::error::(I18N-CATALOG-GATE) $LINGUI is missing; run 'bun install' first"
	exit 1
fi
"$LINGUI" extract --clean --overwrite --workers 1
"$LINGUI" compile --strict --workers 1

if ! git diff --quiet -- packages/i18n/locales ||
	[ -n "$(git status --porcelain -- packages/i18n/locales)" ]; then
	echo "::error::(I18N-CATALOG-GATE) the committed catalogs do not match what the source extracts to. A message missing from the catalog renders as its hashed id (e.g. OGXtL8) in a production build. Run 'bun run check:i18n', fill in any new translations, and commit packages/i18n/locales."
	git --no-pager diff --stat -- packages/i18n/locales
	git --no-pager diff -- packages/i18n/locales | head -n 200
	exit 1
fi

echo "(I18N-CATALOG-GATE) catalogs match the source"
